name: Chicken Tomato Rice
instructions: Wash and dice the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced onions and minced garlic; sauté for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add diced chicken, salt, and black pepper. Sear until chicken begins to brown (about 5 minutes).
Stir in chopped tomatoes and rinsed rice, mixing well to coat the grains.
Pour in 600ml of water or chicken broth. Bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly with a lid, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: Garnish with fresh parsley or squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top for brightness.

name: Spicy Chicken Fried Rice
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat.
Add minced garlic, sliced onions, and chopped fresh chilies; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add thinly sliced chicken and cook until fully opaque and browned (4-5 minutes).
Add cold cooked rice and break up any clumps with a spatula.
Drizzle soy sauce and sprinkle chili powder over the rice.
Toss vigorously over high heat for 3 minutes until steaming and slightly charred.
Serve hot immediately.
tips: Day-old cold jasmine rice yields the best texture without turning mushy.

name: One-Pot Chicken Rice
instructions: Marinate chicken thighs in soy sauce, grated ginger, and minced garlic for 10 minutes.
Heat a deep pot over medium heat and sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Add washed, drained rice to the pot and stir for 1 minute with the pan juices.
Pour chicken broth over the rice and arrange chicken thighs on top.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and lower heat to simmer for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat, keep covered for 10 minutes to steam, then garnish with scallions.
tips: Substitute bone-in chicken thighs for even richer broth flavor.

name: Classic Egg Sandwich
instructions: Whisk eggs with salt and black pepper in a small bowl.
Melt butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Pour eggs into the skillet and gently scramble until soft curds form (about 2 minutes).
Toast bread slices until golden brown.
Layer the scrambled eggs and cheese between the toasted bread slices.
Slice diagonally and serve immediately.
tips: Add fresh spinach or sliced avocado for extra nutrition.

name: French Toast
instructions: In a shallow dish, whisk together eggs, milk, and ground cinnamon.
Dip bread slices into the mixture, letting each soak for 20 seconds per side.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook bread slices for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drizzle with honey and serve warm.
tips: Brioche or thick-cut stale sandwich bread works best.

name: Vegetable Tomato Pasta
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Cook pasta according to package instructions (approx. 9-11 min) until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, salt, and oregano. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Drain pasta and reserve 50ml of cooking water.
Toss pasta directly into the tomato sauce, adding reserved water if needed for silky coating.
Garnish with basil or chili flakes and serve.
tips: Add red pepper flakes if you prefer an Arrabbiata spicy profile.

name: Spicy Tomato Garlic Pasta
instructions: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; drain and save 1/4 cup pasta water.
In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and chili flakes; sizzle for 90 seconds.
Add crushed tomatoes and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until aromatic and rich.
Fold in drained pasta with pasta water and stir vigorously for 1 minute.
Serve piping hot.
tips: Top with freshly grated parmesan or nutritional yeast for vegan cheese flavor.

name: Creamy Dal Tadka (Lentil Curry)
instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly. Boil in 600ml water with turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt for 20 minutes until soft.
In a small pan, heat oil. Add cumin seeds; let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and garlic; sauté until golden brown.
Add diced tomatoes and remaining salt; cook until tomatoes break down into a paste.
Pour the aromatic tadka (tempering) over the cooked lentils and stir gently.
Simmer together for 3 minutes and serve with steamed rice or flatbread.
tips: Add fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice at the end.

name: Chicken Wrap
instructions: Slice chicken into strips. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Pan-fry chicken in olive oil over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until cooked through.
Mix yogurt with minced garlic and a pinch of salt to make a quick garlic sauce.
Warm the tortillas slightly in a dry pan.
Spread garlic yogurt sauce, layer lettuce, sliced tomatoes, and warm cooked chicken.
Fold the sides in and roll tightly into a wrap.
tips: Toast the finished wrap seam-side down for 1 minute for a crispy exterior.

name: Fruit and Honey Yogurt Bowl
instructions: Spoon fresh Greek yogurt into a serving bowl.
Slice banana and arrange on top alongside washed fresh berries.
Scatter chopped almonds over the fruit for crunch.
Drizzle with honey and serve chilled.
tips: Substitute maple syrup or agave nectar for a vegan alternative with plant-based yogurt.

name: Hearty Oatmeal with Fruit
instructions: Combine oats and liquid in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.
Simmer for 4-5 minutes until creamy and thickened.
Transfer to a bowl, top with sliced banana, a dash of cinnamon, and sweetener.
tips: Add a spoonful of peanut butter for extra protein.

name: Tofu Vegetable Stir Fry
instructions: Press tofu with paper towels to remove excess moisture and cut into bite-sized cubes.
Heat sesame oil in a wok. Fry tofu cubes for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, toss in minced garlic, ginger, and mixed vegetables (broccoli, carrots, peppers). Stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Return crispy tofu to the pan, pour over soy sauce, and toss thoroughly for 1 minute.
Serve warm over steamed rice or noodles.
tips: Coat tofu lightly in cornstarch before pan-frying for maximum crunch.

name: Authentic Chicken Biryani
instructions: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, chili powder, turmeric, and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes.
Wash basmati rice and boil in salted water with whole spices until 70% cooked (about 6 minutes); drain.
In a heavy bottom pot, heat ghee and fry onions until deep golden brown. Set half aside for garnish.
Add marinated chicken to the pot and sear over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Layer the partially cooked basmati rice over the chicken. Sprinkle caramelized onions, chopped mint, and cilantro on top.
Seal the pot with foil and a tight lid (dum style). Cook on very low heat for 20 minutes to allow the steam to infuse the layers.
Gently fluff the rice and chicken from bottom to top and serve with cucumber raita.
tips: Soak a few strands of saffron in warm milk and drizzle over the rice before sealing for radiant golden color and royal aroma.

name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
instructions: Cut chicken into chunks, season with chili powder, ginger-garlic paste, and salt, and sear in a pan with 1 tbsp butter until lightly charred (6-8 minutes). Set aside.
In the same skillet, melt remaining butter. Add minced ginger and garlic; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in tomato puree and simmer for 10 minutes until oil begins to separate.
Stir in garam masala, sugar, salt, and heavy cream, whisking until a silky, velvety orange sauce forms.
Add cooked chicken pieces back into the gravy and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Crush kasuri methi between your palms and scatter over the curry before removing from heat.
Serve warm with garlic naan or basmati rice.
tips: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is the secret restaurant ingredient that gives butter chicken its distinctive signature taste.

name: Pan-Seared Lemon Garlic Salmon with Asparagus
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels; season both sides with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Melt butter and olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side up and sear undisturbed for 4 minutes until a crisp golden crust forms. Flip carefully.
Toss trimmed asparagus spears into the pan around the salmon fillets.
Add minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, and lemon slices into the bubbling butter; spoon the garlic lemon butter continuously over the salmon.
Cook for another 3-4 minutes until salmon flakes easily with a fork and asparagus is tender-crisp.
Serve immediately with pan juices drizzled over top.
tips: Do not move the salmon during the first 4 minutes of searing to guarantee a restaurant-quality crispy crust without tearing.

name: Classic Street Beef Tacos
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and break it apart with a spatula.
Cook for 5-6 minutes until browned; drain excess fat if needed.
Sprinkle chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt over the beef. Stir in 50ml water and simmer for 3 minutes until rich and coated.
Warm tortillas on a dry griddle or skillet for 30 seconds per side until pliable and slightly charred.
Spoon seasoned beef into the center of each warm tortilla.
Top with diced raw onions and fresh cilantro.
Serve hot with fresh lime wedges for squeezing.
tips: Double up on corn tortillas street-taco style to prevent juices from soaking through.

name: Shakshuka (Poached Eggs in Spiced Tomato Pepper Sauce)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a cast-iron or heavy skillet. Sauté chopped onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes until tender.
Add minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and salt; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Use the back of a large spoon to create 4 small wells in the bubbling sauce.
Crack an egg gently into each well.
Cover skillet and cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain gloriously runny.
Scatter crumbled feta and fresh parsley over the top. Serve hot with crusty bread for dipping.
tips: Do not overcook the eggs; pull the skillet off the heat while yolks still have a gentle wobble as residual heat finishes cooking.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions: Soak paneer cubes in warm water for 10 minutes so they remain pillow-soft.
Melt butter in a skillet. Sauté finely chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden.
Add tomato puree, chili powder, and salt. Simmer for 8 minutes until thickened and fragrant.
Stir in heavy cream and garam masala to form a luxurious, smooth gravy.
Drain paneer cubes and gently fold into the simmering gravy. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Finish with crushed kasuri methi and serve alongside hot roti or jeera rice.
tips: Soaking paneer in warm salted water before cooking prevents it from turning rubbery.

name: Classic Fluffy Pancakes
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
In a separate cup, whisk egg, milk, and melted butter.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir gently until just combined. A few small lumps are perfectly fine.
Heat a lightly greased non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter for each pancake. Cook until bubbles appear on the surface and edges look set (about 2-3 minutes).
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm stacked high with butter and maple syrup.
tips: Do not overmix the batter! Overmixing develops gluten and makes pancakes tough rather than fluffy.

name: Warm Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Grease two ramekins and dust with cocoa powder.
Melt dark chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water (or microwave in 20-second bursts). Stir until smooth.
Whisk eggs and sugar together vigorously in another bowl until pale and slightly frothy.
Fold melted chocolate mixture into the eggs, then gently sift in the flour and vanilla.
Divide batter evenly between the prepared ramekins.
Bake for exactly 11-12 minutes until the edges are firm and center is soft and jiggly.
Let cool for 1 minute, run a knife around edges, invert onto plates, and dust with powdered sugar.
tips: Watch the baking time closely! Even 2 extra minutes will turn the molten center into standard cake.

name: Tender Ribeye Steak With Garlic Butter
instructions: Take steaks out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to bring them to room temperature. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
Season generously on all sides with coarse sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot. Add olive oil and swirl to coat the pan.
Carefully lay the steaks in the skillet. Sear undisturbed for 3-4 minutes until a deep golden, caramelized crust forms.
Flip steaks. Immediately add butter, crushed garlic cloves, and fresh rosemary/thyme sprigs to the skillet.
Tilt the pan slightly and use a large spoon to continuously baste the bubbling garlic-herb butter over the top of the steaks for 2-3 minutes (aim for 54°C / 130°F internal for medium-rare).
Transfer steaks to a cutting board and rest for 5-7 minutes before slicing against the grain to keep all the delicious juices inside.
tips: Resting the meat is critical! Slicing too early will cause all the flavorful juices to pour out onto the board.
